entries.title: Auxiliary cutoff Gaussian elastic model
entries.statement: Let P_L(k)=kk^t/|k|^2, P_T=I-P_L, and S_mu(k)=T*1_(0<|k|<=Lambda)*[P_T/(|k|^2*(mu+kappa*|k|^2))+P_L/(a*|k|^s+b*|k|^2)], with T,Lambda,a,mu>0, b,kappa>=0, 0<=s<2 and |k|^0=1. This defines Gaussian displacement increments in R^2, with Fourier measure dk/(2*pi)^2; theta=curl(u)/2, C6_mu(x)=E exp(6i*(theta(x)-theta(0))) and C_G_mu(x)=E exp(i G.(u(x)-u(0))). The microscopic identification with any Riesz gas is an open proof obligation.
assumptions: Two-dimensional real centered Gaussian auxiliary model, not a constructed Riesz Gibbs point process
Fourier measure dk/(2*pi)^2 and disk ultraviolet cutoff 0<|k|<=Lambda
T,Lambda,a>0; 0<=s<2; b>=0; exact covariance specified in the statement
mu>0; kappa>=0

entries.statement: AUXILIARY MODEL ONLY: scoped KEEP audits by w544 and w545; coordinator admission pending. This model therefore cannot have an algebraic sixfold correlation tending to zero; this does not refute a Riesz-gas hexatic phase.

entries.title: DRAFT: bounded-window correlation agreement can hide a plateau
entries.statement: SCOPED KEEP AUDITS by w544 and w545; different-login provenance unverified; retained as a draft concept pending coordinator admission. Let T,Lambda,kappa,mu>0 and define C6_mu(x)=exp[-9T integral_(|k|<=Lambda)(1-cos(k.x))/(mu+kappa|k|^2) dk/(2*pi)^2] and C6_0(x)=exp[-(9T/kappa) integral_(|k|<=Lambda)(1-cos(k.x))/|k|^2 dk/(2*pi)^2]. For every R>0 and |x|<=R, 0<=log(C6_mu(x)/C6_0(x))<=9T*mu*R^2*log(1+kappa*Lambda^2/mu)/(8*pi*kappa^2). The bound tends to zero as mu->0, while each fixed mu>0 has the positive plateau (1+kappa Lambda^2/mu)^[-9T/(4*pi*kappa)]. Meanwhile log C6_0(rn)=-9T log r/(2*pi*kappa)+O(1). Thus arbitrarily good finite-window agreement with algebraic orientation is insufficient to prove the infinite-distance regime.
assumptions: Two-dimensional Gaussian angle increment correlations with disk ultraviolet cutoff
T,Lambda,kappa,mu,R>0; Fourier measure dk/(2*pi)^2
The massless angle model is auxiliary and has no established Riesz-process identification

entries.title: DRAFT: shear-zero angle increments do not construct displacement increments
entries.statement: SCOPED KEEP AUDITS by w544 and w545; different-login provenance unverified; retained as a draft concept pending coordinator admission. In R^2 let the infrared-cutoff transverse Gaussian displacement covariance be T*P_T(k)/(kappa|k|^4) on epsilon<|k|<=Lambda, where P_T=I-kk^t/|k|^2, T,kappa,Lambda>0, with Fourier measure dk/(2*pi)^2. For fixed nonzero G,x, -log E exp[i G.(u_epsilon(x)-u_epsilon(0))]=T*(|G|^2|x|^2+2*(G1*x2-G2*x1)^2)*log(1/epsilon)/(32*pi*kappa)+O(1). Adding a longitudinal covariance T*P_L/(a|k|^s+b|k|^2), a>0,b>=0,0<=s<2, changes only the bounded remainder. The displacement increment variance diverges even though curl-angle increment correlations have a finite massless limit. Setting shear to zero does not construct an ordinary displacement field or a particle Gibbs phase.
assumptions: Fixed nonzero G,x; epsilon decreases to zero
T,kappa,Lambda>0; allowed longitudinal parameters a>0,b>=0,0<=s<2

entries.title: DRAFT: missing microscopic defect reduction for P0321
entries.statement: OPEN PROOF OBLIGATION, not a theorem: for a precisely specified classical two-dimensional Riesz jellium (especially V_0=-log|x| or V_1=1/|x|, with a uniform neutralizing background), construct a nonempty coupling interval and a thermodynamic Gibbs state, and derive a compact orientational angle description that includes dislocations and disclinations. Approximation errors must be uniform in separation and small relative to the decaying bond correlations. The reduction must establish short-range positional order and algebraic sixfold orientational order for named microscopic observables. Gaussian elastic identities and finite-size fits alone do not supply this reduction. Current openness of the full P0321 problem is UNKNOWN; the source describes a qualitative expectation.
assumptions: Density rho>0 and coupling Gamma=beta*rho^(s/2)
Precise Gibbs limits and microscopic correlation observables must be fixed

The positive-shear model has transverse spectrum T*P_T/[k^2*(mu+kappa*k^2)]; the zero-shear claim instead imposes an infrared cutoff on T*P_T/(kappa*k^4). They share projectors and Fourier convention, but are different increment constructions.

The window claim gives arbitrarily small finite-range error; the plateau claim gives a positive infinite-distance limit for every fixed positive shear. Their coexistence is the diagnostic obstruction.
The existing P0321 card asks for an intermediate Riesz hexatic regime; this card identifies the missing microscopic and thermodynamic bridge, and does not claim to solve it.
